headline: OpenAI launches $230 light-up keyboard for AI coding agents
summary: The limited-run 'Codex Micro' features customizable keys and a dial to adjust agent reasoning, aiming to streamline AI workflows.
details: OpenAI has officially entered the hardware market with the release of the Codex Micro, a $230 light-up keyboard designed in collaboration with Work Louder. This device is intended to provide a novel interface for users of its AI coding assistant, Codex, and other AI agents.

The keyboard features unique "Agent Keys" that visually indicate the status of AI agents, along with customizable "Command Keys" for quick access to frequent Codex actions. A joystick is included for launching common workflows, and a dial allows users to adjust the "reasoning level" of agents, controlling their computational effort.

OpenAI positions the Codex Micro as a "command center for agentic work," allowing users to manage their AI coding bots more directly than through traditional desktop or mobile applications. The device is controllable and customizable via the ChatGPT desktop app.

This keyboard is described as a limited-run collaboration, suggesting it's more of a novelty or a statement piece signaling OpenAI's foray into hardware rather than a mass-market product. The company is also reportedly developing a more substantial hardware device, a portable, screenless smart speaker with moving parts, designed by former Apple engineers.

The development of OpenAI's hardware comes amid a legal battle with Apple, which is suing OpenAI for alleged trade secret theft. Apple claims OpenAI's leadership deliberately extracted confidential information to develop its own hardware, a charge OpenAI denies.
